entries.english:
(Co-)Plaintiff/applicant/intervenor: Hans Wilhelm von Grumbach zu Burggrumbach and Estenfeld
(Co-)defendant/intervenor: Konrad von Grumbach zu Rimpar and his nephew Eberhard Friedrich von Grumbach zu Gleißenberg
Plaintiff’s procurators: Dr. Leonhard Wolf (1586); Lic. Johann Peter Mörder (1607)
Defendant’s procurators: Dr. Malachias Ramminger (1570); Lic. Jakob Erhardt (1583); Dr. Christoph Behem (1588); Dr. Erhard Kalt (1590); Dr. Georg Melchior Kirwang (1592); Lic. Jakob Streitt (1593); Dr. Sigismund Haffner (1598)
Subject of dispute (contemporary): citatio ad videndum se restitui
Subject of dispute (modern): restitution suit concerning disadvantage in the division of an inheritance;
In mid-1577, at the request of his nephew Eberhard Friedrich von Grumbach, Konrad von Grumbach divided the estate of Eberhard’s father Karl von Grumbach with Carl’s then-underage brother Hans Wilhelm von Grumbach. At the end of 1577 he acquired the properties assigned to his adult nephew.
At the beginning of 1586 Hans Wilhelm von Grumbach brought a restitution suit: Konrad von Grumbach had divided the paternal estate into two very unequal lots, one containing disputed properties and unprofitable fields, moreover without the necessary labor services, while the other comprised secure rents and tithes and productive fields and meadows; in a sham drawing of lots he had received the less favorable Estenfeld lot, additionally burdened by litigation arising from his father or his uncle Hessel von Grumbach: with Bishop Julius of Würzburg over his uncle’s fiefs (see file no. 781), with his widow Barbara von Heßberg, née von Seckendorff, over his will (see file nos. 6133 and 6640), with Konrad von Rosenberg, Hans Sebastian von Bieberehren, Joachim von Seckendorf, and Wolf Lochinger von Archshofen over a suretyship for Hessel von Grumbach (see file no. 6130), with Wilhelm von Heßberg over a debt claim, with Hans Gotfried von Berlichingen over his wife Amalie von Grumbach’s paternal inheritance, a younger sister of the plaintiff (see file no. 6134/1), and with Sippo Mockema over the inheritance of the plaintiff’s grandfather Friedrich von Grumbach (see file no. 6136); despite his minority, his guardian Hans Fuchs von Dornheim had not been involved in the division, and by their purchase agreement uncle and brother had also overridden his brotherly right of pre-emption. Eberhard Friedrich von Grumbach initially disputed the Imperial Chamber Court’s jurisdiction: the division agreement provided for arbitration in disputes. On the merits, later also Konrad von Grumbach argued that Hans Wilhelm von Grumbach and his mother Sophia von Grumbach had willingly agreed to the division; the two lots had been prepared within a quarter-year by Caspar Hogst, bailiff at Fladungen and experienced in this matter; Konrad Geyer von Giebelstadt and Konrad Voit von Rieneck had also attended the division; Sophia von Grumbach had insisted that her underage son receive Estenfeld; he had sold his inherited properties because of their distance from his seat at Gleißenberg; and his plaintiff brother had not asserted his right of pre-emption within one year.
When, from 1592 onward, Konrad von Grumbach sold properties at Versbach to the Julius Hospital in Würzburg because of debts, the seat at Bibergau to Eberhard von Weitershausen, and finally most of his possessions to Bishop Julius of Würzburg, Hans Wilhelm von Grumbach requested in October 1593 that Count Georg zu Castell be appointed sequestrator and in August and October 1594 requested penal mandates against his uncle’s creditors and the bishop.

Instances: Imperial Chamber Court 1586–1617 (1586–1612)

Documents include: certificate by Heinrich Dülcken, pastor of Burggrumbach, concerning the plaintiff’s birth in 1560 (Q 8); original inheritance-division agreement between Eberhard Friedrich and Hans Wilhelm von Grumbach, 1577 (Q 15); enfeoffment charter of Bishop Melchior of Würzburg for the brothers Carl and Hessel von Grumbach over tithe shares at Sulzwiesen, Erbshausen, Waigolshausen, rents at Seligenstadt and Hergolshausen, and properties at Retzstadt and Güntersleben, 1545 (Q 23); inventory of the Schlosshof, Röttleshof, and Kleinerblein at Estenfeld with associated meadows made for the 1577 division and yields 1578–1589 (Q 24); inventory of Sophia von Grumbach’s widow’s estate gardens (Q 25); arbitral award between Prior Konrad (Zerrer) and the Carthusian convent at Würzburg and Karl von Grumbach concerning disputes over Estenfeld, especially the meal court and bailiwick, 1507 (Q 27); purchase agreement with Konrad von Grumbach concerning Eberhard Friedrich von Grumbach’s paternal inherited properties, especially at Burggrumbach, Unterpleichfeld, Rimpar, and Versbach, 1577 (Q 33); lots for Estenfeld and Burggrumbach compiled for the 1577 division (Q 34, 35).

Contains note: Register: beginning of proceedings 1586.
